text: Funny how nobody in power says it out loud, but the numbers don't lie: they're being shipped in by the millions to replace us. Our grandkids will be strangers in the land their ancestors built.
note: Great-replacement dehumanising coded narrative against migrants

text: It's always the same rootless cosmopolitan crowd pulling the strings behind the banks and the media. They have no homeland, just an appetite for ours.
Lovely 'enrichment' for our neighbourhood. Five kids per family, on our taxes, and in two generations the town won't be ours anymore. Just doing the maths.
note: 'They breed' replacement framing dehumanising via fertility

text: We really do need to protect our bloodline before it's diluted into nothing. Once the native stock is gone, there's no getting it back.
The globalists know exactly what they're doing: open the borders, flood the cities, and watch the host population dissolve. It's not a conspiracy, it's the plan.
note: 'Globalists flooding to dissolve host' coded replacement

text: They don't migrate, they swarm. One hops the fence, then the whole hive follows, and the wage you used to earn vanishes.
Notice how every 'humanitarian' charity airlifting these people in is funded by the same handful of financiers? Almost like there's a parasite class that profits from drowning us in newcomers.
Demographics is destiny. Keep importing them at this rate and within fifty years the people who founded this country are a tolerated minority in their own home. Wake up.
note: Replacement panic engineered to incite against migrants

text: I think this course oversimplifies the economics of immigration. Higher net migration can suppress wages in some low-skill sectors short term, even if it's a long-run positive. The data is genuinely mixed and the lecturer should have said so.
note: Policy critique of immigration economics, no dehumanisation

text: Honestly the way some politicians talk about 'invaders replacing us' is just recycled great-replacement propaganda, and naming that for what it is matters. Coded language is still hate.
note: Counter-speech naming and condemning the dog-whistle

text: My grandmother survived a genocide where the first step was always the same: call the targets vermin, then a disease, then a plague. By the time the killing starts the words already did the work.
note: Personal account explaining dehumanisation, not enacting it

text: I'm genuinely scared about the housing crisis. Rents in my city have doubled and I don't know how my generation is supposed to ever afford a home. It feels hopeless some days.
note: Speaker's own economic anxiety, no targeted group

text: Frankly the entire central banking system is a parasitic racket that funnels wealth upward and leaves working people with the bill. Abolish the Fed.
note: Anti-institution rant, 'parasite' on a system not ethnicity

text: This lecture's segment on 'demographic replacement theory' was useful precisely because it shows how a real statistic about birth rates gets weaponised into a sinister story about a hidden enemy. Great breakdown of the rhetorical trick.
note: Analytic discussion of the trope as object of study
